---
title: "A history of Transformers and LLMs"
subtitle: "From attention mechanisms to contemporary language models"
lang: en
---

This page provides historical landmarks for understanding how attention mechanisms, the Transformer architecture, and different pretraining strategies contributed to modern LLMs. It complements the [conceptual Transformer overview](transformer.qmd), but is not a prerequisite for reading it or following the build path.

This is a selective chronology. It distinguishes precursors, architectural proposals, publications, and public releases. The years refer to the first cited publication or announcement, not necessarily the date of invention or the beginning of adoption.

## Timeline

:::: {.history-timeline}

::: {.history-milestone}
**2014 · Research publication**

### Attention for neural machine translation

Bahdanau, Cho, and Bengio propose an attention mechanism for a recurrent encoder-decoder model. It learns to weight the input parts relevant to each generation step. Attention is therefore a precursor to the Transformer, not an invention of the 2017 paper.

Primary source: [Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.0473).

**Explore the concept:** [scaled dot-product attention](scaled-dot-product-attention.qmd) — a conceptual comparison, not an assertion that this early mechanism is identical to Transformer attention.
:::

::: {.history-milestone}
**2015 · Research publication**

### Multiple formulations of attention

Luong, Pham, and Manning study different scoring functions and ways of computing attention for neural machine translation. Their work illustrates that several variants and design choices existed before the Transformer.

Primary source: [Effective Approaches to Attention-based Neural Machine Translation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.04025).

**Explore the concept:** [scaled dot-product attention](scaled-dot-product-attention.qmd).
:::

::: {.history-milestone}
**2017 · Research publication**

### The Transformer: an attention-based architecture

Vaswani and colleagues present an encoder-decoder architecture for translation whose central mechanism relies on attention rather than recurrence or convolution. The paper formalizes scaled dot-product attention and multi-head attention.

Primary source: [Attention Is All You Need](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762).

**Explore the concepts:** [Transformer overview](transformer.qmd) · [attention](scaled-dot-product-attention.qmd).
:::

::: {.history-milestone}
**2018 · Research publications**

### Two pretraining paths: GPT and BERT

GPT explores autoregressive generative pretraining with a decoder-style Transformer. BERT uses an encoder-style Transformer and a masked-token prediction objective. They share architectural building blocks, but differ in context access and training objective.

Primary sources: [Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training (GPT)](https://openai.com/index/language-unsupervised/) · [BERT](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.04805).

**Explore the concepts:** [causal masking](causal-masking.qmd) · [training examples](training-examples.qmd).
:::

::: {.history-milestone}
**2019 · Publications and public release**

### Scaling and context handling

GPT-2 studies text-conditioned generation and zero-shot transfer, with a staged public release of the model. In parallel, Transformer-XL introduces recurrence across segments to handle dependencies beyond a segmented context window. These works address different questions: scale and transfer on one hand, context length on the other.

Sources: [GPT-2 announcement and report](https://openai.com/index/better-language-models/) · [Transformer-XL](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.02860).

**Explore the concepts:** [positional encoding](positional-encoding.qmd) · [causal masking](causal-masking.qmd).
:::

::: {.history-milestone}
**2020 · Research publications**

### Few-shot behavior and extension to other modalities

GPT-3 studies the *few-shot* behavior of large language models conditioned on examples in the prompt. In the same year, Vision Transformer applies Transformer blocks to sequences of image patches. ViT is not an LLM; it illustrates the extension of the architecture to another modality.

Primary sources: [Language Models are Few-Shot Learners](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165) · [An Image is Worth 16x16 Words](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.11929).

**Explore the concepts:** [contextualized representations](contextualized-representations.qmd) · [Transformer overview](transformer.qmd).
:::

::: {.history-milestone}
**2022 · Research publication and public launch**

### Human-preference training and conversational interface

InstructGPT studies model tuning for better instruction following, including the use of demonstrations and human preferences. ChatGPT was subsequently made available to the public as a conversational interface. This is an important milestone in diffusion and use, not the invention of Transformers or preference learning.

Sources: [Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155) · [ChatGPT announcement](https://openai.com/index/chatgpt/).

**Explore the concept:** [experimental evaluation](experimental-evaluation.qmd). The site does not yet have a dedicated lesson on preference alignment.
:::

::::

## How to read this chronology

- **Attention and Transformer are not synonyms.** Attention mechanisms existed before 2017; the Transformer proposed one particular architecture.
- **Transformer and autoregressive LLM are not synonyms.** The 2017 paper describes an encoder-decoder model for translation; BERT follows a distinct encoder path.
- **Development paths are parallel.** Encoder, decoder, encoder-decoder, multimodal models, and alignment methods address different objectives.
- **Scale does not explain everything.** Data, objectives, tokenization, architecture, training procedure, and evaluation protocol all contribute to observed behavior.
- **A publication date does not establish absolute priority.** This pedagogical selection does not catalogue every parallel contribution or every stage of adoption.
